name: CMR Green Technologies Ltd
title: CMR Green Technologies Ltd - 544777 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Recycled aluminium leader with FY26 volume up 24% to 80,381 t and EBITDA up 50% to INR449 cr, but no quantified guidance and capex of about INR200 cr for FY27 with capacity rising to about 7 lakh t.

capex.quote: FY27, the capex, actually we already about INR200 crores is the capex that we're doing in FY27.

summary.headline: FY26 consolidated revenue rose 30% to INR 8,640 crore and EBITDA 50% to INR 449 crore, at about INR 11,000 per ton.
summary.overview: CMR Green Technologies reported FY26 consolidated revenue of INR 8,640 crore (up 30% YoY), EBITDA of INR 449 crore (up 50%, 5.2% margin, about INR 11,000/ton) and PAT of INR 228 crore (up 47.3%). Q4 FY26 revenue was INR 2,364 crore (up 45%), EBITDA INR 128 crore (up 160%, 5.4% margin) and PAT INR 65.68 crore. Total volume grew 24% to 80,381 metric tons, with aluminium up 27% and non-aluminium up 18%. Management said capacity will rise from about 6.15 lakh tons to nearly 7 lakh tons by FY27, with the Shoolagiri and Bawal plants coming online this year. The company listed on NSE and BSE on 10 June 2026 via a INR 630 crore pure offer for sale.

segments.name: Aluminium (liquid metal, ingots, billets, sheet ingots)
segments.commentary: About 80-81% of revenue; 65,636 MT sold in FY26 (+27%). Customers are mainly auto OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers, with liquid metal supplied on single-source terms.

segments.name: Non-aluminium (stainless steel, zinc, lead, copper, brass, magnesium)
segments.commentary: About 19-20% of revenue; 14,745 MT in FY26 (+18%), growing quarter-on-quarter. Customers include Jindal Stainless and Aurubis (Germany).

guidance_outlook: Capacity to rise from about 6.05 lakh MT to nearly 7 lakh MT by end-FY27, split about 80% aluminium and 20% non-aluminium.
FY27 capex of about INR 200 crore.
Management expects volume growth similar to FY26's 25% in FY27 and a good year in FY28, without quantifying it.
EBITDA per ton expected to keep improving, with no numeric target given. Management said EBITDA should be assessed per ton, not as a percentage of turnover.
Aluminium/non-aluminium mix could move toward 75:25 from 80:20 over time, per management.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity about 6.15 lakh MT per annum today across 13 plants; newly operational Tirupati and Jharsuguda units are being ramped up.
Shoolagiri (Future Mobility Park, Tamil Nadu) plant under construction and Bawal (Haryana) second plant under construction; both expected to start operations in FY27.
Management is evaluating a new billets and sheet ingots plant after the first facility ramp-up went well.
Carbon credit stock of 2.73 lakh tons, unrecognised in revenue; accumulating 70,000-80,000 tons per year.
demand_pricing: Auto sector volumes reportedly grew 12% in the first two months of FY27 (per management); EV +18%, two-wheelers +12%.
Management said prices are hedged and pass-through is monthly, so commodity moves should not hit profitability; aluminium prices spiked after the Iran-US conflict.
Scrap sourcing spans six continents plus domestic; UAE has a four-month export ban; EU proposed a 15% scrap export duty from September 2026 and a non-OECD export ban from May 2027.
EPR mandate for recycled content starts FY29 at 5-10%, rising to 60-70% in some products (per management).
Management claimed about 45% share of the auto aluminium market and said CMR gained share each year from FY22.

qa_highlights.question: What capacity will be available by end-FY27, and what is the aluminium/non-aluminium split?
qa_highlights.answer: About 6.05 lakh MT now, rising to nearly 7 lakh MT by FY27; roughly 80% aluminium and 20% non-aluminium.

qa_highlights.question: What are EBITDA per ton for aluminium and non-aluminium, and what margin targets exist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not split them because scrap is sourced together; blended EBITDA was about INR 11,000+/ton in FY26 and should keep improving, with no number given.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is budgeted for FY27 and what volume growth is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 200 crore of FY27 capex. Volume growth of about 25% is expected to be similar in FY27, with FY28 also described as a good year.

qa_highlights.question: Will aluminium realisations hold if commodity prices ease?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pricing is monthly pass-through and positions are hedged, so profitability should be maintained. It did not address the price outlook in detail.

qa_highlights.question: Why are other recyclers not adding capacity, and how confident is the EPR adoption?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it cannot comment on competitors and that EPR targets should be met given large recycling volumes and design-for-recycling trends.

qa_highlights.question: Why did volumes at a key customer lag, and what is the import competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disputed the premise and said CMR gained share each year, citing Craftsman share rising 2-3x. Imports are small and concentrated in South India, and liquid metal locks customers in.

qa_highlights.question: How is the OCI of INR 166 crore arising, and how does hedging work?
qa_highlights.answer: The OCI is mark-to-market on cash-flow hedges covering exposure from day one to day 60 under monthly pricing; it will reverse as physical prices move.

risks_watch: Scrap export bans or duties (UAE, EU, US, Mexico) could restrict feedstock; the company said the complex scrap India uses should keep flowing.
Commodity price volatility after the geopolitical spike; hedging is used, but a hedged OCI of INR 166 crore sits on the balance sheet until it settles.
Ramp-up of the new Tirupati, Jharsuguda, Shoolagiri and Bawal plants, and whether 7 lakh MT is reached in FY27.
EBITDA per ton trajectory: management gave no numeric target.
Customer concentration and volume growth at key auto accounts; a questioner cited flat volumes at one customer since FY22.
Management did not give a timeline or details for the Hindustan Zinc zinc alloy MoU.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, ESG and market leadership, but guarded on forward numbers: no EBITDA/ton or margin targets were given and several questions on realisations and competition were deflected. Answers ran long and the call was cut short by the moderator.
key_quotes: So, we are like both a owner -run and a professional organization into one.

In the auto sector, we have nearly a 45% market share, which means that more or less every second vehicle that you see on the road, be it a two-wheeler or a four-wheeler, it's made from aluminum supplied from CMR.
We buy on day one, we sell on day 100.
We deliver them 24 hours a day directly online.

adds.what: Shoolagiri (Future Mobility Park, Tamil Nadu) plant
Capacity rising from ~6.15 lakh MT to nearly 7 lakh MT by end-FY27 (~80% aluminium, 20% non-aluminium)

growth.why: Management expects FY27 volume growth similar to FY26's ~25%, backed by capacity rising from ~6.15 to nearly 7 lakh MT by end-FY27 via Shoolagiri and Bawal plants under construction and ~INR 200 crore FY27 capex, though plant-level timing and volume-to-capacity linkage are only partly quantified.
